a benefit.en: something helpful or good that you get from something

a coincidence.en: a surprising situation in which two things happen together by chance

a convention.en: a usual or accepted way of doing something

a delay.en: a period of time when something is late or waits

a forecast.en: a statement about what is expected to happen in the future

a habit.en: something a person does regularly, often without thinking

a method.en: a particular way of doing something

a pattern.en: a regular way in which something happens or is arranged

a procedure.en: a set of steps for doing something in an accepted way

a rarity.en: something that is unusual and not often found or seen

a remedy.en: something that cures a problem or illness

a reprieve.en: a temporary relief or delay from something unpleasant

a routine.en: a usual, regular way of doing things

a solution.en: a way of solving a problem

a summary.en: a short statement of the main points

ambiguity.en: the quality of having more than one possible meaning

ambiguous.en: having more than one possible meaning; unclear

an aberration.en: something that is different from what is normal or expected

an anomaly.en: something unusual that does not fit the normal pattern

an exception.en: something that does not follow the general rule

an incident.en: an event, especially an unusual or unpleasant one

argument.en: a disagreement; or a set of reasons supporting an idea

beneficial.en: having a good or helpful effect

classified.en: arranged things into groups (past tense of classify)
classified.zh: 分類（classify 的過去式／過去分詞）

complicate.en: to make something more difficult to understand or deal with

conceal.en: to hide something or keep it secret

confusion.en: a state of not understanding clearly

contradicted.en: said or showed that something is not true

controversy.en: a lot of public disagreement about something

costly.en: costing a lot of money or causing loss

criticize.en: to say what is bad or wrong about someone or something

decorative.en: meant to look attractive rather than to be useful

delayed.en: made something happen later than planned

democratize.en: to make something available to all people

diminish.en: to make or become smaller or less important

disastrous.en: very bad; causing great harm or failure

distracted.en: took someone's attention away from what they were doing

distraction.en: something that takes attention away from what you should focus on

effective.en: producing the result that is wanted

formalize.en: to make something official or give it a fixed structure

guided.en: directed or influenced the way something developed

hesitation.en: a pause or delay because you are unsure

hostility.en: unfriendly or aggressive feelings or behavior

improbable.en: not likely to happen or be true

incidental.en: happening by chance as a minor side effect, not by design

influenced.en: had an effect on how someone or something developed

informed.en: gave information to; shaped or guided (work or ideas)

inspired.en: gave someone the idea or the desire to create something

interrupted.en: stopped something for a short time; broke in

irrelevant.en: not related to the matter being discussed

isolation.en: the state of being alone or separated from others

limited.en: kept something within a certain size or range

novelty.en: the quality of being new and unusual; something new

obscure.en: not well known; or difficult to understand

obscured.en: made something hard to see or understand

popularize.en: to make something liked or used by many ordinary people

praise.en: to express approval or admiration of

prestige.en: respect and admiration that comes from success or high status

productive.en: producing a lot or achieving good results

publicize.en: to make something widely known to the public

rejected.en: refused to accept or believe something

renown.en: the state of being famous and admired

replace.en: to put something new in place of something else

reputation.en: the general opinion people have about someone or something

respect.en: admiration for someone because of their qualities or achievements

shaped.en: influenced the form or development of something

sincerity.en: the quality of being honest and meaning what you say

spread.en: to cause to reach a wider area or more people

standardize.en: to make things the same according to a fixed standard

standing.en: a person's position or reputation in relation to others

suspicion.en: a feeling that someone is guilty or that something is wrong

symbolic.en: serving as a symbol; representing something else

temporary.en: lasting for only a limited time

thoughtfulness.en: the quality of being considerate of others or thinking carefully

uncertainty.en: the state of not being sure

weaken.en: to make or become less strong
